threatModel.observerKnows: the list of n students and the amount approved for each
threatModel.allowedSources: ONLY the Withdraw events and the contract state
threatModel.forbiddenSources: MongoDB, IPFS, note contents, private witnesses
threatModel.note: The university is OUTSIDE this model - it is the sender of the transactions and therefore already knows everything. C1 only has meaning against a THIRD PARTY observing the chain.
threatModel.collusionModel: Attack path 3 additionally models COLLUDING WITHDRAWERS, as required by ISO/IEC 15408-2 (CC:2022) FPR_UNL.1 Annex I.4.2.2. Each withdrawer privately knows their own nullifier, so a coalition can subtract ITSELF from the candidate set of any withdrawal it did not make.
threatModel.collusionAssumption: WORST CASE, not average: every other withdrawer in the run is assumed to collude. Chosen because it is deterministic - no random choice of coalition - so the number is reproducible across runs.
threatModel.orderingChannel: Attack path 4 models an observer who knows the SUBMISSION order and guesses that the i-th withdrawal on chain belongs to the i-th applicant. This channel exists because `onlySchool` routes every withdrawal through a single account, so one nonce sequence fixes the on-chain order to the backend's disbursement order.
threatModel.orderingMitigation: The university SHUFFLES the approved requests before disbursing (scenario.shuffleWithdrawOrder, default on). This is an OPERATIONAL policy, not a cryptographic guarantee - a deployment that disburses in submission order leaks identity through ordering even when every grant carries the same amount.
threatModel.orderingMeasurementCondition: Ganache auto-mines one transaction per block, so block order is fully visible. On a real chain several withdrawals share a block and intra-block order is the proposer's choice, making this channel weaker. Both block_number and tx_index are reported.
threatModel.amountTiersModel: scenario.amountTiers splits the n students into a few amount levels by share, assigned with a fixed seed. The observer still knows every approved amount, so the anonymity set of a withdrawal is the number of students in its level, not n.
threatModel.walletReuseModel: scenario.walletReuseProbe opens a SECOND pool of the same university after the withdrawals and asks Student Affairs to register, for that many students, the wallet they were paid to in the first pool, then one fresh wallet as a control. A refusal means the system itself prevents the cross-pool link.
threatModel.collusionBound: A coalition can only remove ITSELF. Students whose approved amount matches but who did NOT withdraw in this run stay in the candidate set, so the anonymity set never reaches zero and shrinks by at most (withdrawerCount - 1).

refusalMessages: Wallet address is already used by another scholarship (pool 6ad8fad5af52349374794e92). Each scholarship program needs its OWN address: reusing one lets an observer link the two payouts and shrinks the anonymity set. Register a NEW address.
